params.body:
Third step for `site`, `vuln` and `pages` at once. A round over the fleet this evening wrote verdicts on every measured row of the three (site 2 facets, vuln 3, pages 8), so the rule next to each line goes.

- Site (Response, Certificate), Packages (the runtime/packages ladder, malware), Pages and SEO (tags, broken, missing, extras, thin, robots), Links and Speed take the word Elixir gave the facet. A facet Elixir did not judge (an old row, or hoet-design-web, which did not measure this evening) is `background`, never `ok`, and the card says "not yet".
- Numbers left in these cards: none. The 8 days, the 1200 ms and the severity ladder are Elixir's now. The Judged line no longer counts as a cause in a card's verdict sentence ("Pages and Judged need attention").
- Docs: the paper's "one truth" section carries the 2026-09-12 move and the rule that a threshold number in Portal PHP is a defect; the fleet-brief contract no longer speaks of cards that still judge.

Tests: 13 older test classes built rows from facts alone and leaned on the card to judge (HerstelKnop, FleetBrief, IngestPlaybook, IngestTask, LaunchList, WorkAge, Brief, MalwareOpDeKaart, NietOnzeProductie, Triage, VerdictSentence, FleetChanges, WorklistLedger). They now use `Tests\Support\JudgedRows`, a small double that writes onto such a row what Elixir writes for the same facts, documented as a double of Elixir's registry for those three keys. The card tests per measurement keep explicit verdicts and do not use it. Suite green except the worktree-only `BuildStampTest`; PHPStan and Pint clean.

With this, every card the plan listed with hardcoded numbers (deployed, app, credentials, site, vulns, pages) is migrated. What still judges in PHP maps a word Elixir wrote, or belongs to measurements not yet moved (the server CPU lines in Speed).
params.title: No card holds a threshold number of its own
